metadata.passing_grade_conditions: Students shall take all assessments and examinations and must have an attendance of not less than 80% in the class. In case of lacking output or examination, a grade of INC (Incomplete) shall be given in accordance with the existing rules and regulations reflected in the student handbook. In case of incurring absences of more than 20% of the total expected number of attendances, a grade of UW (Unauthorized Withdrawal) will be reflected in the grade sheet.

sdg_table.description: Microprocessors and microcontrollers are foundation technologies for industrial automation, smart devices, and digital infrastructure. Arduino-based system design fosters innovation and practical engineering skills.

The course includes history and evolution, principles, and applications of microprocessors. The focus is on the basic understanding of the architectural design, functional parts, operations, function, and programming. It also covers the study of various types of microprocessors and the fundamental concepts of microcontrollers.

syllabus_assessment_activities.description: Oral recitations require students to explain and analyze the functional operations of microprocessors and microcontrollers—such as ALU processing, control unit sequencing, and instruction execution—using Arduino-based examples. Emphasis is placed on articulating how these internal operations support the development of reliable and innovative embedded systems used in modern infrastructure and smart community applications.

Group activities engage students in the collaborative design, implementation, and troubleshooting of Arduino-based microcontroller systems involving data movement, control logic, and I/O interfacing. Through teamwork and hands-on system development, students simulate real-world engineering practices while creating embedded solutions relevant to intelligent infrastructure and sustainable community technologies.

Quizzes assess students’ ability to analyze and solve problems related to microprocessor/microcontroller structures, instruction sets, and functional operations. These assessments reinforce the foundational knowledge required to develop dependable microcontroller-based systems that underpin innovative industrial applications and efficient, technology-driven urban environments.

The term examination comprehensively evaluates students’ understanding of microprocessor and microcontroller principles through problem-solving, analytical, and design-oriented questions centered on Arduino-based systems. Students are expected to integrate theoretical concepts and practical reasoning to demonstrate how embedded systems contribute to innovative technological infrastructure and sustainable, smart community solutions.

metadata.workload_description:
With 18 weeks at 2 contact hours per week (36 contact hours total), the expected student workload is as follows:
• Total of 4 quizzes (2 for both Midterm and Final Term)
• Post-discussion oral recitation or group activity
• Midterm and Final Examinations
In instances where face-to-face sessions are impractical, simulated experiments or their equivalent will be provided.
